description: PULSE is a multidisciplinary team developing an innovative health-monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Combining biomedical science, engineering, artificial intelligence, and software development, we aim to transform health data into meaningful insights to support astronaut well-being and advance the future of human space exploration.
summary:
PULSE is a digital health-monitoring platform designed to support astronauts in monitoring and understanding their health during space missions. It addresses the challenges of limited medical access in space, where microgravity and other space-related conditions can affect the human body.

We developed an interactive, responsive website featuring health-monitoring tools, guided self-assessments, health history tracking, medical guidance, and interactive 3D anatomical models to help astronauts better understand different body systems. We also integrated an Arduino-based prototype with environmental sensors to demonstrate real-time data collection and alerts.

PULSE aims to make health monitoring more accessible, organized, and informative, allowing astronauts to perform guided checks and keep track of changes in their health. By combining technology, accessible medical information, and sensor integration, PULSE contributes to safer, more informed, and sustainable human space exploration.
details:
PULSE is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to address the medical challenges astronauts face during space missions. Microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, and changes in the space environment can affect multiple body systems. Since immediate access to medical professionals is limited in space, astronauts need accessible tools to monitor their health and recognize potential changes.

How It Works

PULSE combines a digital health platform with a physical hardware prototype. The website provides astronauts with guided health assessments covering different body systems, including vision, brain and nervous system functions, immunity, and bone health. These assessments use interactive instructions and self-evaluation activities to help astronauts monitor changes in their health. The platform also allows users to record results, review their health history, and access AI-assisted guidance to better understand health-related questions.

In addition, we developed an Arduino-based prototype incorporating an MQ-6 gas sensor to demonstrate environmental gas detection. This introduces an additional layer of environmental awareness alongside personal health monitoring.

Benefits and Intended Impact

PULSE aims to:

  • Make health monitoring more accessible and organized during space missions.
  • Help astronauts identify potential changes in their health through regular assessments.
  • Maintain health records that allow astronauts to observe changes over time.
  • Provide accessible guidance when direct medical assistance is limited.
  • Demonstrate how hardware and software can work together to support astronaut safety.

Our long-term vision is to contribute to safer human space exploration by supporting astronauts in taking a more active role in monitoring their health.

Technology and Development Tools

We used several technologies to develop PULSE:

  • React and TypeScript: Developing the interactive website and its functionality.
  • HTML and CSS: Structuring and styling the platform.
  • JavaScript: Supporting interactive features and application logic.
  • Arduino Mega 2560: Developing the physical prototype.
  • MQ-2 Gas Sensor: Demonstrating environmental gas detection.
  • Visual Studio Code: Writing, editing, and managing the project's code.
  • GitHub: Supporting code management and version control.
  • Web deployment tools: Making the platform accessible online.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes PULSE creative is its combination of digital health assessments, interactive visual experiences, AI-assisted guidance, health-history tracking, and physical sensor integration within one platform. Rather than focusing on a single health concern, PULSE takes a broader approach by considering multiple body systems and the environment astronauts operate in.

Factors Considered

Throughout development, we considered the unique conditions of space, the limitations of medical access, the importance of simple and understandable instructions, data organization, accessibility, and adaptability across laptops, tablets, and mobile devices. We also considered the need for a user-friendly interface that astronauts can navigate independently, even in demanding mission environments.

PULSE is our attempt to bring together healthcare, engineering, and technology to help make future space exploration safer and more sustainable.
